title: Co-extraction of RNA and DNA from animal tissue
author: Dominik Buchner

steps.title: Prepare bead-filled screwcap tube
steps.instruction: Place a 2 mL screw‑cap tube in a rack and add approximately 400 mg of 2 mm zirconia beads together with 0.1 mm glass beads (about one small spoon of each type).

steps.title: Add animal tissue to tube
steps.instruction: Add up to 30 mg of animal tissue (10 mg is typical) to the tube. Use less tissue for samples with very high RNA content.

steps.title: Add lysis buffer and optional reagents
steps.instruction: Pipette 1000 µL of GITC lysis buffer into the tube. If desired, add 10 µL of 2‑Mercaptoethanol (note: this requires fume‑hood handling). If foam forms during bead‑beating, add silicone antifoam to the lysis buffer at 30 ppm.

steps.title: Bead‑beat sample to homogenize
steps.instruction: Immediately bead‑beat the tube for 5 minutes (00:05:00) at maximum speed, adjusting the time as needed until the tissue is completely homogenized.

steps.title: Centrifuge lysate to clear debris
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the lysate at x g, room temperature, for 10 minutes to obtain cleared lysate.

steps.title: Bind DNA to silica column
steps.instruction: Transfer 700 µL of the cleared lysate to a silica spin column (DNA column) and keep the flow‑through. Mark the column as DNA column. If only RNA is required, discard this column now.

steps.title: Prepare RNA binding mixture with ethanol
steps.instruction: Add 700 µL of 70 % ethanol to the flow‑through from the previous step, vortex to mix (do not centrifuge).

steps.title: Load RNA mixture onto silica column
steps.instruction: Load the ethanol‑mixed lysate onto a second silica spin column (RNA column). Centrifuge at 11 000 × g, room temperature, for 15 seconds and discard the flow‑through. Repeat the loading step once more to pass the entire volume through the column.

substeps.instruction: Load mixture onto RNA column and centrifuge 15 s.
Repeat loading to transfer remaining volume.

steps.title: Wash RNA column with wash buffer 1
steps.instruction: Add 700 µL of RNA wash buffer 1 to the RNA column, centrifuge at 11 000 × g, room temperature, for 15 seconds and discard the flow‑through.

steps.title: Wash RNA and DNA columns with wash buffer 2
steps.instruction: Add 500 µL of RNA wash buffer 2 to the RNA column and 500 µL of DNA wash buffer 1 to the DNA column, then centrifuge both at 11 000 × g, room temperature, for 15 seconds and discard the flow‑through.

substeps.instruction: Add 500 µL RNA wash buffer 2 to RNA column.
Add 500 µL DNA wash buffer 1 to DNA column.

steps.title: Final wash of RNA and DNA columns
steps.instruction: Add 500 µL of RNA wash buffer 2 to the RNA column and 500 µL of DNA wash buffer 2 to the DNA column, centrifuge at 11 000 × g, room temperature, for 15 seconds and discard the flow‑through.

substeps.instruction: Add 500 µL RNA wash buffer 2 to RNA column.
Add 500 µL DNA wash buffer 2 to DNA column.

steps.title: Dry silica membranes
steps.instruction: Spin each column at 11 000 × g, room temperature, for 1 minute to dry the silica membrane, then transfer each column to a fresh 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube.

steps.title: Elute nucleic acids from columns
steps.instruction: Add 100 µL of elution buffer directly onto each silica membrane, incubate at room temperature for 3 minutes (00:03:00). The elution volume may be adjusted between 30 µL and 200 µL as needed.

steps.title: Centrifuge and store RNA and DNA
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the columns at 11 000 × g, room temperature, for 1 minute to collect the eluate. Store the RNA eluate at –80 °C and the DNA eluate at –20 °C. If DNA‑free RNA is required, treat the RNA with DNase and clean up with an RNA‑cleanup protocol.

substeps.instruction: Optional: DNase treat RNA for DNA‑free preparation.
